source_text: Haec sunt, ut arbitror, genera doctrinarum adulterinarum, quae sub apostolis fuisse ab ipsis apostolis discimus. Et tamen nullam invenimus institutionem inter tot diversitates perversitatum quae de deo creatore universorum controversiam moverit. Nemo alterum deum ausus est suspicari. Facilius de filio quam de patre haesitabatur, donec Marcion praeter creatorem alium deum solius bonitalis induceret, Apelles creatorem angelum nescio quem gloriosum superioris dei faceret deum legis et IsraÃ«lis, illum igneum affirmans, Valentinus Aeonas sues spargeret et unius Aeonis vitium in originem deduceret dei creatoris. His solis et his primis revelata est veritas divinitatis, maiorem scilicet dignationem et pleniorem gratiam a diabolo consecutis, qui deum sic quoque voluerit aemulari, ut de doctrinis venenorum, quod dominus negavit, ipse faceret discipulos super magistrum. Eligant igitur sibi tempora universae haereses quae quando fuerint, dum non intersit quae quando, dum de veritate non sint, et utique quae sub apostolis non fuerunt, fuisse non possint. Si autem fuissent, nominarentur et ipsae, ut et ipsae coercendae essent. Quae vero sub apostolis fuerunt, in sua nominatione damnantur. Sive ergo eaedem nunc sunt aliquante expolitiores quae sub apostolis rudes, habent suam exinde damnationem: sive aliae quidem fuerunt, aliae autem postea obortae quasdam ex illis opiniones usurpaverunt, habendo cum eis consortium praedicationis habeant necesse est etiam consortium damnationis, praecedente illo fine supradicto posteritatis, quod etsi nihil de damnaticiis participarent, de aetate sola praciudicarentur, tanto magis adulterae quanto nec ab apostolis nominatae. Unde firmius constat has esse quae adhuc tunc nuntiabantur futurae.
thought_title: Heresies under the apostles and the late revelation of false gods
orientation: Tertullian is surveying the heretical doctrines that existed in apostolic times and arguing that the major heresies about the creator God arose only later.
pass_a_gloss: These are, as I think, the kinds of adulterous doctrines, which we learn from the apostles themselves to have been under the apostles. And yet we find no teaching among so many diversities of perversities which moved a controversy about the God creator of all things. No one dared to suspect another god. More easily was there hesitation about the Son than about the Father, until Marcion introduced besides the creator another god of goodness alone, Apelles made the creator some glorious angel of the higher god, I do not know which, the god of the law and of Israel, affirming him to be fiery, Valentinus scattered his own aeons and led down the fault of one aeon into the origin of the god creator. To these alone and to these first was revealed the truth of divinity, to those who obtained, that is, a greater condescension and a fuller grace from the devil, who wished to rival God in this way also, so that from the teachings of poisons, which the Lord denied, he himself would make disciples above the master. Let all heresies choose for themselves, then, the times when they existed, provided it does not matter which when, provided they are not of the truth, and certainly those which were not under the apostles cannot have been. But if they had been, they themselves would be named, so that they themselves also would have to be restrained. Those, however, which were under the apostles, are condemned in their own naming. Therefore either the same ones are now somewhat more polished which were rough under the apostles, they have their condemnation from that time: or some indeed were, but others arose afterwards and usurped certain opinions from them, by having with them a partnership of preaching they must necessarily have also a partnership of condemnation, with that end of later origin mentioned above preceding, because even if they shared nothing of the condemnable things, by age alone they would be prejudged, so much the more adulterous as they were not even named by the apostles. Whence it stands more firmly that these are the ones which were being announced at that time as still future.

choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of adultery, which Tertullian uses throughout for false teaching that corrupts the faith.

choices.english: about the God creator of all things
choices.why: Preserves the full title Tertullian gives to the creator God, emphasizing his role as maker of the universe.
rejected: about God the creator of the universe

choices.why: Literal rendering of the genitive of quality, capturing Marcion's claim that his god is characterized solely by goodness.
rejected: a different god who is only good

choices.term: angelum nescio quem gloriosum superioris dei
choices.english: some glorious angel of the higher god, I do not know which
choices.why: Preserves the dismissive 'nescio quem' and the word order, showing Tertullian's contempt for Apelles' teaching.
rejected: a certain glorious angel of the higher god
some glorious angel of the superior god

choices.why: Keeps the vivid verb 'spargeret' and the possessive, reflecting Valentinus' proliferation of aeons.
Literal rendering of the genitive, preserving the metaphor of heretical doctrine as poison.

pass_b_english: These are, I think, the kinds of adulterous doctrines which we learn from the apostles themselves existed in their own time. And yet among so many varieties of perversity we find no teaching that raised a controversy about the God creator of all things. No one dared to suspect another god. There was more hesitation about the Son than about the Father, until Marcion introduced another god of goodness alone besides the creator, and Apelles made the creator some glorious angel of the higher god, I do not know which, the god of the law and of Israel, affirming him to be fiery, and Valentinus scattered his own aeons and derived the origin of the creator god from the defect of one aeon. To these alone, and to these first, was the truth of divinity revealed—they obtained, of course, a greater favor and a fuller grace from the devil, who wished to rival God in this way too: from the teachings of poisons he would make disciples above their master, something the Lord denied (Matthew 10:24). Let all heresies choose for themselves the times when they existed, since it does not matter which time, as long as they are not from the truth; and certainly those which were not under the apostles could not have existed then. If they had existed, they would also have been named, so that they too might have been checked. Those which did exist under the apostles are condemned in their very naming. Therefore, whether the same ones are now somewhat more polished which were crude under the apostles, they have their condemnation from that fact; or whether some were different, and others arose afterward and usurped certain opinions from them, by sharing in their preaching they must necessarily share also in their condemnation, since that principle of lateness mentioned above precedes them—even if they shared nothing of the condemned doctrines, they would be judged by their age alone, all the more adulterous because they were not even named by the apostles. From this it is established more firmly that these are the ones which were even then being announced as still to come.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'sues' means 'swine/pigs', not 'his own'. Valentinus scattered swine-like aeons, a derogatory image.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin likely 'suis' (his), not 'sues' meaning pigs; translation 'his own aeons' matches intended meaning.

last_rejected.why: Context is ironic: the 'truth about the divine nature' was supposedly revealed to these heretics first, implying orthodox churches lacked it.
last_rejected.ruling: ‘veritas divinitatis’ literally ‘the truth of divinity’; translation conveys meaning, nuance not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: from the teachings of poisons he would make disciples above their master
last_rejected.source_quote: ut de doctrinis venenorum, quod dominus negavit, ipse faceret discipulos super magistrum
last_rejected.why: 'quod dominus negavit' means 'which the Lord denied'—the devil makes disciples contrary to what the Lord taught, not 'something the Lord denied.'
last_rejected.fix: from the teachings of poisons he would make disciples above their master, which the Lord denied
last_rejected.ruling: ‘quod dominus negavit’ = ‘which the Lord denied’; translation captures this with ‘something the Lord denied’.
